clinical.citation: ASHG 2017 - De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects. (Slavotinek A, Risolino M, Losa M, et al.)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo heterozygous variants; functional studies demonstrated abnormal cellular processes including perturbation of PBX-dependent transactivation, altered nuclear translocation, and abnormal interactions with TALE/HOX cofactors; phenotype resembles Pbx1 mutant mice
clinical.center_country: Multiple centers (USA, Australia, Netherlands); includes UCSF, University of Groningen, Sydney Children's Hospital among others

model_organism.citation: Requirement for Pbx1 in skeletal patterning and programming chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation (PMID: 11566859)
phenotypes: Severe hypoplasia or aplasia of multiple organs
Widespread patterning defects of axial and appendicular skeleton
Malformations of proximal limb skeletal elements
Neural crest cell-derived skeletal structures of second branchial arch transformed into first arch-derived cartilage elements
Markedly diminished chondrocyte proliferation in affected domains
Precocious expression of Col1a1 (marker of bone formation)

model_organism.citation: Loss of PBX1 function in Leydig cells causes testicular dysgenesis and male sterility (PMID: 38724675)
phenotypes: Altered fate decisions of progenitor Leydig cells
Altered transcription of genes associated with testosterone synthesis
Increases in pregnenolone, androstenedione, and luteinizing hormone
Dysregulated expression of Prlr, Nr2f2, and Nedd4

model_organism.citation: PBX1-directed stem cell transcriptional program drives tumor progression in myeloproliferative neoplasm (PMID: 34678207)
phenotypes: Absence of thrombocythemia and granulocytosis in JAK2V617F background without PBX1
Erythrocytosis initially present but gradually resolved over time
Absence of cytokine-independent growth in vitro
Reversion of aberrant transcriptome in stem/progenitor cells from MPN model

model_organism.citation: Essential role for Pbx1 in corneal morphogenesis (PMID: 19797217)
phenotypes: Corneal dystrophy apparent in newborns, progressively worsening with age
Stromal infiltration with atypical basal cells
Severe disorganization of stromal collagen matrix

model_organism.citation: A PBX1-IL7R axis mediates liver fibrosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (PMID: 40885520)
phenotypes: Significant attenuation of liver fibrosis induced by CDAA-HFD feeding
No influence on liver injury or steatosis

model_organism.citation: Meis1, Hi1α, and GATA1 are integrated into a hierarchical regulatory network to mediate primitive erythropoiesis (PMID: 34496088)
Targeting TNF/IL-17/MAPK pathway in hE2A-PBX1 leukemia: effects of OUL35, KJ-Pyr-9, and CID44216842 (PMID: 38385270)
phenotypes: Increased myeloid differentiation propensity of hematopoietic stem cells
Activation of TNF/IL-17/MAPK signaling pathway in blood cells

model_organism.citation: Prep1, A Homeodomain Transcription Factor Involved in Glucose and Lipid Metabolism (PMID: 30002646)
phenotypes: Age-dependent overt diabetes mellitus in trans-heterozygous Pbx1+/-Pdx1+/- mice

model_organism.citation: RNA-Binding Protein Hnrnpa1 Triggers Daughter Cardiomyocyte Formation by Promoting Cardiomyocyte Dedifferentiation and Cell Cycle Activity in a Post-Transcriptional Manner (PMID: 39559922)
phenotypes: Inhibited cardiac regeneration in neonatal MI model
Worsened cardiac function after myocardial infarction
Reduced Pbx1 expression (as downstream target of Hnrnpa1/Mettl3 pathway)
Decreased cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation and cell cycle activity

model_organism.citation: Meis2 controls skeletal formation in the hyoid region (PMID: 36247013)
phenotypes: Severely reduced expression of PBX1 in the hyoid region (as downstream consequence of Meis2 cKO)
Aberrant hyoid apparatus with complete skeletal chain from neurocranium base to lesser horns

biological.citation: Cicero Predicts cis-Regulatory DNA Interactions from Single-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Data (PMID: 30078726)
biological.summary: In differentiating myoblasts, a subset of DNA elements bound by MYOD1 exhibit early chromatin opening in a PBX1- and MEIS1-dependent manner. PBX1 acts as a pioneer factor facilitating chromatin accessibility at regulatory elements that form 'chromatin hubs' coordinating gene regulation during myoblast differentiation.

biological.citation: Pre-B-cell leukemia transcription factor 1 contributes to liver fibrosis by enabling IL-7 signaling in HSC (PMID: 40080840)
biological.summary: PBX1 was identified as the most prominently upregulated transcription factor during hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation in liver fibrosis. PBX1 knockdown attenuated HSC-to-myofibroblast transition in vitro and liver fibrosis in mice, acting via transcriptional activation of IL7R/CD127 to promote pro-fibrogenic signaling. Notch3 was shown to mediate PBX1 upregulation at the transcriptional level in HSCs.

biological.citation: PBX1-promoted SFRP4 transcription inhibits cell proliferation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in endometrial carcinoma (PMID: 37054536)
biological.summary: PBX1 and SFRP4 are downregulated in endometrial carcinoma cells; overexpression of PBX1 suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. PBX1 directly bound the SFRP4 promoter (confirmed by ChIP and luciferase assays) and promoted its transcription, thereby inhibiting Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation and the EMT process.

biological.citation: Molecular Mechanisms of Lupus Susceptibility Allele PBX1D (PMID: 37486226)
biological.summary: The dominant-negative splice isoform PBX1D, which lacks DNA- and Hox-binding domains, is more frequently expressed in CD4+ T cells from lupus-prone mice and SLE patients. PBX1D is less stable than PBX1B due to ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation at K292-K293, and is retained in the cytoplasm without MEIS/PREP1 cofactors, impairing regulatory T cell homeostasis and expanding inflammatory CD4+ T cells.

biological.citation: The histone lysine acetyltransferase HBO1 (KAT7) regulates hematopoietic stem cell quiescence and self-renewal (PMID: 34724565)
biological.summary: Pbx1 is among the genes essential for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) quiescence and self-renewal that are downregulated in HSC-enriched cell populations after conditional deletion of Hbo1 in mice. HBO1-mediated H3K14 acetylation at the Pbx1 locus is required for its expression, placing PBX1 within a transcription factor network critical for HSC maintenance.

biological.citation: Pbx1 overexpression delays cochlear hair cells degeneration in an accelerated aging mouse model (PMID: 41581416)
biological.summary: PBX1 expression shows a striking age-dependent reduction in mouse cochlear hair cells. AAV-mediated Pbx1 overexpression in vivo improved auditory function and preserved hair cell structure in an age-related hearing loss mouse model, establishing PBX1 as a key mediator of hair cell aging.

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects (ASHG 2017)
biological.summary: Seven patients with heterozygous de novo PBX1 variants presented with intellectual disability and multi-organ developmental defects mirroring those in Pbx1-/- mice (ear, heart, lung, kidney, diaphragm anomalies). Functional studies on five variants showed impaired PBX-dependent transactivation, altered nuclear translocation, and abnormal interactions with TALE/HOX cofactors, confirming that PBX1 forms multimeric complexes to regulate target gene transcription during development.

biological.citation: ASHG 2013 - Interrogating the PBX-WNT-TP63 pathway in human nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate (ASHG 2013)
biological.summary: Family-based association analyses in 829 NSCL/P families identified PBX1 SNP rs1044263 as associated with nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate in Hispanic multiplex families (p=0.002), providing the first human genetic evidence for PBX1 involvement in craniofacial morphogenesis. This is consistent with the fully penetrant CL/P phenotype observed in Pbx-knockout mice and the Pbx-Wnt-p63-Irf6 regulatory module controlling facial morphogenesis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Analysis of time-series embryonic diaphragm transcriptomes identifies Pbx1 as a candidate gene for diaphragmatic defects (ASHG 2011)
biological.summary: Computational analysis of time-series embryonic mouse diaphragm transcriptomes identified Pbx1 as a top candidate gene for congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Ex vivo examination of Pbx1 knockout mouse embryos at E15.5 revealed diaphragmatic defects in 3/3 animals, validating PBX1 as a CDH-associated gene involved in muscle differentiation and mesodermal patterning.

biological.citation: Aberrant Expression and Oncogenic Activity of SPP1 in Hodgkin Lymphoma (PMID: 40149711)
biological.summary: Aberrantly expressed PBX1, together with HOXB9, mediates transcriptional activation of SPP1 (osteopontin) in Hodgkin lymphoma cell line SUP-HD1, as demonstrated by transcription factor binding site analysis and functional knockdown experiments. This identifies PBX1 as a direct transcriptional activator of an oncogenic cytokine in a B-cell malignancy context.
